tofino.h1: Best time to visit Tofino: crowds, whales, waves and storms
tofino.lede: Tofino works all year, but the crowds do not. Summer is the busiest and most expensive season, spring and fall are quieter, and winter is the quietest, with storm watching as the reason to come.

months.like: Quiet and good value. The Pacific is at its most dramatic, and the Hot Cocoa Trail runs through early January.
Still the quiet season. Early gray whales may begin to appear, though whale tours are limited and storms remain the main draw.
Whale season opens with the Pacific Rim Whale Festival. Tours and rooms are in demand that week, so book early; storms can still roll in.
A shoulder season with fewer crowds. Bears start working the shoreline at low tide and shorebirds arrive for the Tofino Shorebird Festival in late April.
The calm before the July rush. Shorebirds peak until mid-May, and the Rip Curl Nationals surf contest is usually held at Cox Bay.
Peak season begins. Surf lessons and rentals need booking well ahead, and the free Tofino shuttle helps with beach parking from late June.
The busiest and most expensive month. Popular resorts can need booking 6 to 12 months ahead, and tours fill fast.
Still peak. Tours, charters and rooms fill early, surf lineups are crowded, and the beach parking lots fill very early.
Early September is still summer-busy, then crowds thin out. Tables and trailheads get easier, though popular weekends can still fill up.
Moderate crowds and shorter restaurant waits than July. October is Surf Month, and bears make their last boat-tour appearances before hibernation.
Storm season is under way and the coast empties out. Good value for oceanfront stays, with the Hot Cocoa Trail starting in late November.
Quiet and moody, though holidays and some weekends can still be busy. Major gales are most frequent in November and December.

events.name: Pacific Rim Whale Festival
events.what: Whale spotting, a parade, food and talks in Tofino, Ucluelet and the park. 2026: March 14 to 21. 2027: March 13 to 20.

events.name: Herring spawn
events.what: Herring turn the coastal water a milky turquoise and draw eagles, sea lions and even wolves along the shoreline.

events.name: Tofino Shorebird Festival
events.what: Thousands of shorebirds stop at the Tofino mudflats on their northern migration, with guided birding by kayak.

events.name: Rip Curl Nationals
events.what: Canada's top shortboard surfers compete at Cox Bay for national titles and Team Canada qualification spots.

events.name: Tofino Market
events.what: Local makers and food vendors at the Village Green. Arrive before noon, as popular items sell out.

events.name: Queen of the Peak
events.what: An all-women's surf championship celebrating women's and girls' shortboarding and longboarding.

events.name: Surf Month
events.what: October is officially Surf Month in Tofino, with major local surf events and reliable early winter swells.

events.name: Edge to Edge Marathon
events.what: A scenic race along the Wild Pacific Trail and rugged coastline between Tofino and Ucluelet.

events.name: Tofino Hot Cocoa Trail
events.what: A self-guided tour of local cafes and restaurants serving creative takes on hot chocolate.

events.name: Vancouver Island Winter Surf Games
events.what: A rugged winter surf contest that depends on the weather and shows off cold-water dedication.

dress: There is no bad weather here, only poor clothing. Pack a proper waterproof jacket in any month.
Dress in layers: a fleece under the shell. It feels colder on the water, so add more for boat tours.
Wear waterproof shoes or boots on beaches and trails, and water shoes at Hot Springs Cove, where rocks are slippery.
In cooler months add a toque and gloves. Surfers need a 4/3mm or 5/4mm wetsuit, plus booties in winter.

faqs.a: Summer, roughly June through early September, is the busiest and most expensive time. July and August are the peak, and popular resorts can need booking 6 to 12 months ahead.
Winter, from November to February, is the quietest season and the best value, though holidays and some weekends can still fill. Spring and fall sit in between, with fewer crowds than summer.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see whales near Tofino?
faqs.a: Gray whales pass from March to May, and humpbacks are common from summer into fall. The main whale watching season runs March through November, and most tours do not run in winter.

faqs.q: When is storm watching season in Tofino?
faqs.a: The main season runs from November to March, with the most dramatic and frequent storms from November to February. Stay at least two nights for a better chance of seeing a big one.

faqs.q: When is the best time to surf in Tofino?
faqs.a: Surfing is year-round. Summer suits beginners, with smaller waves but crowded lineups. Spring suits intermediates, and fall and winter bring bigger swells for experienced surfers. October is Surf Month.
Cool and ocean-influenced, with mild temperatures all year and wetter months in fall and winter. Dress for it and every season has something to offer.

ucluelet.h1: Best time to visit Ucluelet: crowds, whales, fishing and storms
ucluelet.lede: Ucluelet is quieter than Tofino all year, but it still has a rhythm. Summer is busiest, the March whale festival brings a spring surge, fishing peaks from June to August, and winter belongs to storm watchers.

months.sea: Big storm swells at the headlands
months.like: Quiet for tourism. Winter days are short, so plan storm viewing for roughly 10 am to 3 pm at the lighthouse or trail.
Whale tours are limited, but gray whales can be spotted from the Wild Pacific Trail from February. Storms remain the main draw.
Festival week brings demand for tours and rooms, so reserve ahead. Shore spotting at Amphitrite Point is part of the programming.
One of the best gray whale months, and a quieter one. The Ucluelet Aquarium hosts the Seaweed Festival, with a market and a field day.
Gray whales may still be passing, with mothers and calves often later in the migration. Crowds stay light before summer.

months.sea: Calmer, with a long rolling swell
months.like: Peak season starts and fishing guides begin to fill. Free parking at Amphitrite Point can fill quickly in the peak summer months.

months.sea: Calmer, with a long rolling swell
months.like: The busiest month for wildlife tours and fishing charters. Guides book up months ahead, so start looking in early spring.

months.sea: Calmer, with a long rolling swell
months.like: A strong month for humpbacks and still peak for visitors. Charters book months ahead and popular parking areas fill early.
Early September is still summer-busy, then it thins out. Fall can be excellent for wildlife, with fewer crowds and quieter tours.

months.sea: First big swells and early storms
months.like: Moderate crowds and moodier conditions. Whale tour schedules become more variable, and salmon return to Thornton Creek Hatchery.
Storm season is under way. Not a whale month, but the coast is dramatic and quiet, and oceanfront stays are good value.
A quiet season. The aquarium's Release Day in early December returns the season's residents to the harbour.

events.name: Pacific Rim Whale Festival
events.what: Whale spotting, food events, talks and a hatchery barbecue. 2026: March 14 to 21. 2027: March 13 to 20.

events.name: Herring spawn
events.what: Herring turn the coastal water a milky turquoise and draw eagles, sea lions and even wolves along the shoreline.

events.name: Seaweed Festival
events.what: Hosted by the Ucluelet Aquarium, with a seaweed market and a field day at Big Beach on coastal foraging.

events.name: Ukee Days
events.what: A festival at the Village Green with loggers' sports, a parade and a salmon barbecue.

events.name: Thornton Creek salmon run
events.what: Thousands of salmon return to spawn at the hatchery near Ucluelet, drawing black bears and wolves to the banks.

events.name: Edge to Edge Marathon
events.what: A scenic race along the Wild Pacific Trail and rugged coastline between Tofino and Ucluelet.

events.name: Ucluelet Aquarium Release Day
events.what: The community gathers as the aquarium's residents are returned to the harbour at the end of the season.

dress: There is no bad weather here, only poor clothing. Pack a proper waterproof jacket in any month.
Dress in layers, and add more for boat tours or fishing charters, where it is cooler on the water.
Wear waterproof boots on the Wild Pacific Trail and beaches, and closed-toe shoes on boats. Bring binoculars.
In cooler months add a hat or toque and gloves, and remember that storm viewing is best done in daylight.

faqs.a: Summer is the busiest season, with July and August the peak for wildlife tours and fishing charters. Popular parking areas can fill quickly, and the March whale festival also brings demand for tours and rooms.
Winter is quieter for tourism, from November to February. Spring and fall are in between, and fall in particular can offer fewer crowds with strong wildlife watching.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see whales in Ucluelet?
faqs.a: Gray whales are strongest from March to May, with the peak in March and April. Humpbacks are most common from May through September, and orcas appear sporadically through the year.

faqs.q: When is the best time to fish from Ucluelet?
faqs.a: Chinook salmon peak from June through August, and can also be caught from March to May and in September. October to February is generally quiet. Halibut fishing is consistent.

faqs.q: When is storm watching season in Ucluelet?
faqs.a: The most consistent and powerful storms come from November through February, and October and March can also be impressive. Amphitrite Point and the Wild Pacific Trail are the classic viewing spots.
A mild oceanic climate with cool summers, relatively gentle winters and plenty of rain. Dress for it and every season has something to offer.
